correctness.rationale: All four base points form a geometric frame, giving precisely six components, four ordinary triple and three ordinary double points. The bipartite flag graph has 13 vertices and 18 oriented edges, so its integral kernel is rank six. Reconstructible fundamental cycles give all 24 S4 matrices satisfying all 576 composition identities. Each V4 eigensublattice has a primitive two-column basis, their combined determinant is ±16, and twice its inverse has integer entries, establishing quotient (Z/2)^4. Each of five class representatives is conjugated by an explicitly checked determinant-±1 integer matrix to the listed normal blocks; the torus and rational group descriptions follow over arbitrary q from integral Galois-module classification. The normalization fixed-point formula is separately verified. Critically the proof uses full integer bases, not only finite q experiments.

originality.rationale: The rank-six full S4 integral cycle module has an explicit index-sixteen failure of decomposition into its three primitive V4 eigenplanes, and all five cyclic Frobenius actions admit explicit unimodular normal forms. Geisser provides the abstract Picard-torus cohomological method, not these evaluated specific integral invariants. The closest published six-chord geometry covers a different seven-component curve (with an added conic) and treats moduli/freeness, while the Igusa torus theorem uses fifteen lines and S6. No same-object or stronger published theorem was found in the actual database and literature comparisons; historical priority remains provisional.

value.rationale: The natural Picard torus of the six-side boundary of a projective frame has a specific, nontrivial integral 2-primary gluing between the three rational V4-character summands: the full lattice has index 16 over their primitive sum. This distinguishes integral descent from rational representation data and makes the arithmetic tori and their finite groups explicit across every cycle type; four- and three-cycle twists both have a single rational curve point while their torus groups differ. The exact invariant is tied to intrinsic S4-symmetry and degeneration of a classical degree-six curve, not an arbitrary graph slice.
